A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, and their text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable. V2's Appendices A–B correspond to v3's retained material; v3 additionally includes Appendices C–E.

before.justification: Section 4 and Figures 3–5 report original Gemma 3 experiments comparing contextual and patched generation, including token agreement, logit differences and total variation distance for text and image contexts.

after.justification: V3 retains original Gemma experiments and reports additional Falcon-7B results, layer-depth ablations and scaling-variant comparisons in Appendix C.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 now propagates the actual patched block output instead of the recorded target activation, allowing subsequent patches to compensate for numerical errors. Appendix B's footnote and C.5 also introduce a variant that updates Wdown and rescales m. The core rank-1 construction and existing Stable RMSNorm inversion remain.

E1.justification: V3 identifies four additional constrained-writing, analogy and poetry prompts in Appendix C.1. However, v2 already aggregates unspecified textual generations in Figure 4. Both evaluate text generation and image description, so the PDFs do not establish whether these newly identified prompts expand previous task coverage or disclose existing cases.

E2.justification: Appendix C.5 and Figure 13 add the evaluated Scaling variant alongside the retained naive and Stable updates. The original model with context remains the reference. Falcon supplies an additional evaluation architecture, not a competing method.

E3.justification: V3 adds Falcon-7B evaluation, starting-layer sweeps under both precisions and update variants, and Hellinger, rank, Top-1 and parameter-norm measurements in Appendix C. This substantially expands the evaluation design. The original metrics and matched-history token-forcing procedure are retained.

E4.justification: Beyond v2's precision and stabilization comparisons, v3 investigates patch starting depth, final-layer-only updating, matrix versus vector update magnitudes, and an alternative scaling strategy. Appendix C.2 and C.4–C.5 substantially expand the analysis of numerical failures and update choices.

E5.justification: Both versions show distributions across generated tokens without reporting seeds, repeated-run protocols, confidence intervals or significance tests. V3's five generations correspond to distinct prompts; its additional boxplots extend the existing reporting practice.

E6.justification: Figures 3–5 contain revised Gemma traces and token matches; Section 4.2 changes reported Stable bfloat16 agreement from 98% to 100%. Appendix C adds Falcon matching results, bfloat16 degradation when updating only the final layer, and scaling/norm findings. The algorithm revision and changed image-generation history preclude treating these as controlled same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: Appendix D adds an impossibility theorem for fixed post-RMSNorm scaling, while Appendix E derives trace-loss gradient-step representations of the updates. V3 also introduces explicit nonzero-input/activation qualifications and per-layer conditions in its definitions and theorems. The original controllability lemmas and RMSNorm inversion derivation are largely retained under new numbering.

C1.justification: The abstract and central conditional-equivalence contribution remain essentially unchanged. The introduction and conclusion extend the empirical-validation claim from Gemma to Falcon, while retaining the same principal theoretical contribution.

C2.justification: V2 already acknowledges token dependence and the absence of an immediate efficient-inference algorithm. V3 adds the distinction between representational equivalence and the model actually executing a learning algorithm, an architectural failure boundary, a gradient-step interpretation, and explanations of Falcon's stability and distributed matrix patches in Sections 4–6.

D1.justification: V3 newly specifies argmax generation, aggregation over five textual generations, additional prompt texts and replacing zero denominators with 1. Conversely, it removes the CPU/TPU labels from the Gemma figures. These change reproducibility documentation without establishing changes in hardware or the previously used generation count.

R1.justification: V3 adds Almazrouei et al. (2023) for Falcon and Innocenti and Achour (2025), including a substantive comparison concerning bias-free architectures, normalization and multilayer proofs. It also elaborates the connection to Mazzawi et al.'s thought patches while retaining the existing research positioning.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main section sequence are retained. Local revisions clarify the MLP function and scaling notation, correct theorem/lemma references and replace the misleading 'poem' description with 'forecast'. Dedicated limitations, future-work and disclosure passages are added.

P2.justification: The main text switches to a two-column conference layout with running headers and substantial reflow. Existing figures and Table 1 are resized or relocated, axes and legends are revised, and Figures 6–13 add extensive multi-panel experimental displays.

improvement.justification: V3 substantially strengthens support for the general architectural claim through Falcon validation and ablations that examine numerical failure and patch placement. Explicit assumptions, Appendix D and Section 6.1 also clarify the framework's boundaries, while Algorithm 1 addresses propagation of numerical errors. These gains outweigh limited reporting weaknesses, including removed hardware labels and Appendix C.2's inconsistency between its rank-correlation definition and interpreting near-zero plotted values as agreement.
